facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
On 23 April 2012 five individuals (Mr I. Bakirov, Mr S. Davidis, Ms Y. Lukyanova, Ms N. Mityushkina and Mr S. Udaltsov) submitted notice of a public demonstration to the mayor of Moscow.

The aim of the demonstration notified on 23 April 2012 was to protest against abuses and falsifications in the course of the elections to the State Duma and of the President of the Russian Federation, and to demand fair elections, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the international obligations of the Russian Federation.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square to take part in the demonstration.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
The applicant was found guilty of failure to obey lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant was subsequently charged with participation in mass disorder, a criminal offence provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was subsequently charged with having committed violent acts against police officers, a criminal offence provided for by Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was detained and tried on the charges of participation in mass disorder and violent acts against police officers.
The applicant was convicted to a prison term of two years and three months.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found eight individuals, including the applicant, guilty of participation in mass disorder and of violent acts against police officers during the public assembly on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow in the first Bolotnaya case judgment of 21 February 2014.
The applicant was found guilty of failure to obey lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant was subsequently charged with participation in mass disorder, a criminal offence provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was subsequently charged with having committed violent acts against police officers, a criminal offence provided for by Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence not endangering life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community works for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
The applicant was subsequently charged with participation in mass disorder, a criminal offence provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was subsequently charged with having committed violent acts against police officers, a criminal offence provided for by Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into the suspected mass disorder and violent acts against the police under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

At one point during the dispersal of the demonstration on 6 May 2012, the applicant picked up from the ground a small round yellow object and threw it over the heads of the protesters in the direction of the police.
The applicant was accused of throwing an unidentified small round yellow object that hit police officer F.'s shoulder during the events of 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that the applicant (Mr Belousov) used violence not endangering the life or health of police officer F.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that between 5 p.m. and 8.10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 unidentified participants in the mass disorder deliberately administered at least three blows and kicks to police officer F.'s head, body and limbs, after which the applicant (Mr Belousov) deliberately threw an unidentified solid yellow round object which hit police officer F. on the upper right side of the chest, causing him physical pain.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that as a result of the applicant's (Mr Belousov's) and other unidentified persons' actions, police officer F. sustained physical pain and injuries in the form of bruising and abrasion of the soft tissues of the parietal region, bruising of the left forearm, and abrasion on the right shin, which constituted injuries not endangering life or health and not entailing short-term health impairment or minor durable professional incapacitation.

The applicant (Mr Belousov) pleaded not guilty at trial and testified that he went to Malyy Kamennyy Bridge to see why the meeting was not starting, saw the riot police cordon and officers arresting some participants, was looking to leave, went to the middle of Bolotnaya Square, saw a girl who tripped on something and nearly fell, picked up an object from the ground that felt soft and slimy, threw it away without aiming it at anyone, joined hands with other protesters chanting slogans, and was then grabbed by three police officers and carried to the police vehicle.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court took into account the nature and degree of the applicant's involvement in the mass disorder and considered it possible to give him a sentence below the minimum punishment provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 21 February 2014, calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation partly concurrent with a one-year prison term under Article 318 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
